clue.text: Flowering plant entwined in some latch

indicators.note: things entwined are twisted together, so the letters are wound into a new order

parts.note: nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A climbing plant has wound itself through the latch on a garden gate.
explanation.definitionFit: Moschatel is a small woodland plant with greenish musk-scented flowers, sometimes called town-hall clock.

clue.text: Bungle in classic TV show

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to make a mess of something
second meaning: the long-running American sitcom about an army field hospital in Korea

explanation.surface: Someone fluffs their part in a famous television series.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a mash of a task is to botch it, and M*A*S*H was the celebrated comedy series set in the Korean War.

clue.text: Kept up a lot of commotion about river's tidal feature

indicators.note: in a down entry, something kept up is raised from bottom to top, so it reads upwards
about means placed around, so the shortened word wraps the river letter
a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a fuss is a commotion
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone kept up a great fuss about the tides on a river estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: Shorten first, then turn the result upwards, and only then wrap the river letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Surf is the foaming water of breaking waves along a shore, a feature of the moving sea.

clue.text: I start to ridicule copper in helmet, say — and what it conceals?

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the headgear word

parts.note: a helmet is one kind of hat, as 'say' signals
taken as written

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of ridicule
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A speaker mocks a policeman's helmet and wonders what lies underneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the rest of the clue: 'it' is the helmet, and under a hat lies your trimmed hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat covers the top of the head, so the style of trimmed hair beneath is exactly what it hides.

clue.text: Leave with no standard of measurement fixed in test of branch of geometry

indicators.note: something fixed in is set firmly inside, so the run of words sits within the test word

parts.note: a trial is a test
to go is to leave
taken as written
the metric system is a standard of measurement

explanation.surface: An exam question about shapes asks you to leave out units of measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: Trigonometry, the study of triangles and angles, is a branch of mathematics closely allied to geometry; this is its adjective form.

clue.text: French novel in which male rues England after a disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things wrecked and jumbled, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: fifteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A novel whose hero, a Frenchman, regrets ever crossing to England after some catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Grand Meaulnes is Alain-Fournier's 1913 novel of lost youth, a classic of French literature.

clue.text: Olympic performer several overlooked at the end

indicators.note: overlooking the end of a word means ignoring its final letter

parts.note: divers is an old word for several or sundry

explanation.surface: Several Olympic competitors got passed over in the closing stages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' meaning several survives in phrases like 'divers reasons'; dropping its final S leaves the competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Diving is an Olympic sport, with athletes performing twists and somersaults from springboards and high platforms.

clue.text: Nothing is upset in department's security

indicators.note: in puts the preceding letters inside the department abbreviation

parts.note: DEPT is the usual abbreviation for department
O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the short word reads bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Nobody is bothered about the safety arrangements in an office department.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the word 'is' is turned up; the nothing letter stays in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is money lodged as a guarantee or pledge, which is one sense of security.

clue.text: Against one repeatedly getting cross about English in Disraeli novel

parts.note: V (versus, against) plus I (one), done twice

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the cross word goes around the English abbreviation

parts.note: to be cross is to be angry
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: In a Disraeli novel, a character keeps losing his temper with the English.
explanation.walkthrough: V for versus is the usual crossword shorthand for against; 'repeatedly' asks for the pair twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivian Grey was Benjamin Disraeli's first novel, published in 1826 before his political career took off.

clue.text: Woman's upset about detective initially making a mistake — this isn't a clue

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned over, so the combination reads upwards
about means surrounding, so the woman word goes round the single letter

parts.note: her stands for a woman

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter only of the word before it

parts.note: first letter of detective
erring is making a mistake

explanation.surface: A woman is flustered by a detective blundering in a mystery story.
explanation.walkthrough: The detective story surface makes 'clue' look like evidence, which is the point of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A red herring is a misleading lead planted to throw investigators off, so it is a false clue rather than a real one.

clue.text: Observing last ones in the colony escaping? Securing four still around

indicators.note: securing means holding something fast inside, so the number goes within the shortened word
letters escaping get out of the word, so they are removed from it

parts.note: surveying is observing

indicators.note: the last ones in a group of words are the final letter of each word

parts.note: last letters of the and colony
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone watches the last members of an animal colony fleeing and finds four left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark ends the first sentence of wordplay; 'still around' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Surviving describes something that remains alive or in existence, as in the surviving relatives of the deceased.

clue.text: Father struggled to ignore one with flags

indicators.note: ignoring one means leaving out the letter that stands for one

parts.note: pa is a father
vied means struggled or competed

explanation.surface: Dad battled to pay no attention to one carrying flags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flags' looks like banners, but here they are flagstones.
explanation.definitionFit: A path that has been laid with flagstones, the flat slabs used for walkways, is a paved one.

clue.text: Playing chess to alarm — here's an easy win

indicators.note: playing with something means moving it about freely, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: twelve letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A sly chess player alarms the opponent and grabs a quick victory.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface really is about chess, so the solution sits in the scene; only the anagram is disguised.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholar's mate is a four-move checkmate against a beginner, attacking the weak pawn beside the king with queen and bishop.

clue.text: Nasty of the French, getting sanctimonious over old message

parts.note: des is French for 'of the' with a plural noun
pi is informal for pious or sanctimonious
a cable was a telegram, an old-fashioned message

explanation.surface: Someone nasty about the French grows pious over an old telegram.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' simply means placed above, so the pieces run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Despicable means deserving contempt, so a despicable act is a nasty, mean-spirited one.

clue.text: Very big name adopting one cause mostly about live births

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the letters for one are taken into the very-big-name group
mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: a VIP is a very important person
to arouse is to cause or stir up
V is the abbreviation for very
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A celebrity takes up a cause concerned with childbirth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' belongs to the definition, meaning 'relating to'.
explanation.definitionFit: A viviparous animal bears its young alive rather than laying eggs, so the word relates to live births.

clue.text: Live way out, around far side of forests

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the way-out word encloses the single letter

parts.note: an exit is a way out

indicators.note: the far side of a word is its end, so only its last letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of forests

explanation.surface: People living off the grid, out beyond the edge of the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' could be an adjective, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to be alive or to have being, which is what the verb live means here.

clue.text: Experienced hand not initially more daring when trapping deer

indicators.note: trapping means catching and holding inside
not initially means without the opening letter

parts.note: bolder means more daring
a stag is a male deer

explanation.surface: A veteran hunter shows less bravado when it comes to catching deer.
explanation.walkthrough: BOLDER loses B to give OLDER, which then traps STAG: OLD(STAG)ER.
explanation.definitionFit: An old stager is a veteran who has long experience of some activity, an old hand.

clue.text: Favour support being installed in a lot of toilets

indicators.note: something installed in a fitting is set inside it
a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the last letter goes

parts.note: privies are outdoor toilets
a leg supports a table or chair

explanation.surface: A plumber does a favour by fitting supports in a row of lavatories.
explanation.walkthrough: Privy is an old word for an outdoor lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A privilege is a special advantage or favour granted to someone, as in the privilege of an invitation.

clue.text: Popular directors occupying ship?

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: A well-liked board of directors takes over a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose definition: inboard means within a ship's hull.
explanation.definitionFit: Inboard describes something situated inside a vessel's hull, such as an inboard motor, so it occupies the ship.

clue.text: TV merchandise perhaps that is rolling in money

indicators.note: a person rolling in something is surrounded by it, so the short phrase sits inside

parts.note: tin is old slang for money
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: Television spin-off goods make the producers rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling in money' reads as being rich, hiding its job.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is a product linked commercially to a film or show, so toys based on a television series are an example.

clue.text: Minor transactions Italy needed, running out of time

indicators.note: running out of time means losing the letter that stands for time

parts.note: taken as the abbreviation TR for transactions
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
something vital is needed

explanation.surface: Italy needed some small financial deals as its deadline approached.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the standard abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial means of little importance or significance, which is what minor means as an adjective.

clue.text: Dictionary I caught including Greek letter in smaller-scale notes

indicators.note: including means holding within, so the Greek letter is taken inside the dictionary name

parts.note: Chambers is a well-known British dictionary, the crossword setter's favourite
mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
taken as written
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A smaller dictionary notes that I have caught a Greek letter.
explanation.walkthrough: C for caught comes from cricket scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: Chamber music is written for a small group of players, so its notes are performed on a smaller scale than orchestral works.

clue.text: Movie reflecting part of dream life

indicators.note: a reflection shows things mirrored, so the stretch reads backwards
part of means only a stretch of the following words is used

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of dream and the start of life

explanation.surface: A movie that mirrors part of someone's dream life.
explanation.definitionFit: A film is a motion picture, the ordinary British word for what Americans call a movie.

clue.text: Extra luxurious, with husband absent

indicators.note: absent means missing, so the letter for husband is taken away

parts.note: plush means luxurious
H is the abbreviation for husband, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A luxurious extra for a woman whose husband is away.
explanation.walkthrough: PLUSH loses H, the abbreviation for husband.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an additional advantage or bonus, something extra on top of what was expected.

clue.text: Little area containing zero living things

indicators.note: containing means holding within, so the zero letter goes inside

parts.note: a bit is a little
A is the abbreviation for area
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A small patch of ground has nothing living on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Biota is the collective term for the plants and animals of a region, all of its organisms.

clue.text: Cheerful to study bottle containing intravenous drip

parts.note: to con is to study or learn

indicators.note: containing means holding within, so the drip abbreviation goes inside the bottle word

parts.note: a vial is a small bottle
IV is the abbreviation for an intravenous drip

explanation.surface: A patient tries to stay upbeat while examining the bag on an intravenous drip.
explanation.walkthrough: Con meaning study is an old word, as in conning one's lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Convivial means sociable and festive, describing friendly, jolly company enjoying itself.

clue.text: Relaxed when held in the attention of some Londoners

indicators.note: held in means kept inside, so the word for when goes within

parts.note: heed means attention; Cockney Londoners drop the H
as can mean when

explanation.surface: Some Londoners calm down once they are paid attention.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class East Londoners, famously drop the H at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased means loosened or relieved of tension, so a grip that has eased has relaxed.

clue.text: American laboratory's American mission: blocking defeat

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits inside it, so the mission goes within the defeat word

parts.note: a loss is a defeat
the Alamo was a Spanish mission in Texas, site of the 1836 siege

explanation.surface: A US lab's goal is to stop a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'American' belongs to the wordplay: the Alamo is in Texas.
explanation.definitionFit: Los Alamos National Laboratory in New Mexico is where the first atomic bombs were developed in the Manhattan Project.
